items.title: Report: leaked Microsoft roadmap outlines four tiers of Windows AI hardware
items.content_text: Windows Central reported that slides attributed to Microsoft outline four tiers of Windows AI hardware, spanning consumer PCs to systems intended for demanding local AI workloads. The roadmap reportedly combines local processing with cloud AI, but the information comes from slides shared by an X user and is not a confirmed Microsoft announcement.

items.title: GitHub REST API adds a cost-center lookup for resources
items.content_text: GitHub added a REST API endpoint to look up the cost center associated with a user, organization, repository, or enterprise team. The response returns the cost-center ID and name, simplifying billing and cost-center workflows that previously required scanning cost-center resource lists; access depends on the caller’s role.

items.title: GitHub Copilot becomes available in JetBrains Air
items.content_text: GitHub Copilot is now available in JetBrains Air, where users can delegate coding tasks, work across parallel agent sessions, and review results in context. Cloud tasks can run through Air Teams using the user’s existing Copilot subscription rather than JetBrains AI credits.

items.title: CodeQL 2.27.3 adds Python 3.15 and JSON data-extension support
items.content_text: CodeQL 2.27.3 adds support for Python 3.15 features, JSON syntax for data extensions, C23 bit-precise integers, and query-accuracy improvements. The update also changes the GitHub Actions control-flow graph implementation, which may require developers with custom queries to adjust them.

items.title: Google brings Guided Learning to Classroom and Search and updates K-12 AI controls
items.content_text: Google made Guided Learning globally available in Google Classroom and said it is bringing Guided Learning capabilities to Search, beginning with a pilot in select U.S. schools later in November. Google also plans to make Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search unavailable by default for K-12 student accounts until a school administrator turns them on.

items.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Dreadnode for AI security testing
items.content_text: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Dreadnode, whose automated testing is intended to identify weaknesses in AI models, applications, and agents before deployment. The deal would extend CrowdStrike’s security platform into testing and remediation for AI systems; the cited announcement does not disclose a purchase price.

items.title: Snowflake adds governed business context and controls for enterprise AI agents
items.content_text: Snowflake announced new enterprise-agent capabilities, including Business Ontology for approved definitions of business terms and expanded Cortex AI Gateway controls. The updates are intended to give organizations more consistent business context and centralized governance as AI agents use company data and services.

items.title: Anthropic opens Messages API message threads beta to speed up long-running agents
items.content_text: Anthropic launched message threads in public beta for the Messages API: after the initial conversation, developers can send only new messages rather than resending the full history. Anthropic says requests of 500,000 to 1 million tokens see about 35% lower median time to first token; the beta is available on Claude Platform, AWS, Microsoft Foundry, and Anthropic-managed Claude on Google Cloud.

items.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, an open-source prototype for provable inference
items.content_text: Anthropic published research on FlashProve, an open-source prototype for cryptographically verifying model inference while keeping model weights hidden. It released code, Lean formalization, and protocol documentation; the work advances inference verification research, though Anthropic identifies it as an intermediate prototype with technical limitations.

items.title: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, a benchmark for AI assistance with everyday tasks
items.content_text: OpenAI introduced LifeVal, a benchmark intended to measure AI performance on practical everyday tasks, extending evaluation beyond conventional question-answering. Its task selection draws on U.S. and international time-use datasets and a demographically representative survey of 3,995 respondents.

items.title: OpenAI plans a security sprint with Cathedral Systems to test and strengthen its defenses
items.content_text: OpenAI said it is planning an internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems, whose researchers will work alongside OpenAI teams using OpenAI models to test and strengthen the company’s systems. The announcement describes the effort as a way to challenge defenses and help protect its platforms.

items.title: OpenAI increases Security Bug Bounty rewards, with exceptional critical findings eligible for up to $172,000
items.content_text: OpenAI raised rewards in its Security Bug Bounty program to encourage independent researchers to report vulnerabilities. It says exceptional critical findings affecting core products such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform can now be eligible for up to $172,000 when bonuses are included.

items.title: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization
items.content_text: OpenAI appointed former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization. He will advise OpenAI leaders and external partners on responsible AI use to strengthen national and cyber security, including work with U.S. allies.

items.title: Google deprecates Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, schedules API routing changes
items.content_text: Google deprecated Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash in the Gemini API and removed them from the AI Studio model picker. Starting December 1, 2026, requests to those model IDs will route to Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, respectively.

items.title: Trajectory raises $45 million to broaden access to AI model training
items.content_text: Trajectory announced a $45 million Series A at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. The company is also making its post-training platform public, aiming to help customers improve models using feedback and task-specific examples.

items.title: Salesforce agrees to acquire voice-agent company Cresta
items.content_text: Salesforce agreed to acquire Cresta, whose platform combines voice agents for complex customer calls with real-time guidance for human representatives and conversation analysis. The deal would bring Cresta’s voice capabilities into Salesforce’s customer-service ecosystem; the official announcement did not disclose the transaction price.

items.title: DeepSeek introduces Creator Mode for creating plugins in its Harness agent
items.content_text: DeepSeek announced Creator Mode for its Harness agent, letting users turn ideas into custom plugins, with examples including a design workspace, a sandbox game, and a 3D visualizer. It extends the agent’s customization capabilities and adds to DeepSeek’s push into agent products.

items.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 multimodal model for long-horizon agent tasks
items.content_text: Meituan released LongCat-2.5, a native multimodal model with 1.6 trillion total parameters and about 48 billion active per token, aimed at sustained agent work such as complex coding tasks. It was available through Meituan’s chat service and API, with GitHub and Hugging Face releases described as planned rather than already available.

items.title: Microsoft plans locked-down Copilot Chat mode for Study and Learn
items.content_text: Microsoft is preparing an IT-controlled mode that locks Copilot Chat to the Study and Learn Agent, designed for educational settings. Students would not be able to switch to general Copilot Chat or other agents, while still being able to add their own files as references.

items.title: GitHub security risk assessments now show repository protection status
items.content_text: GitHub’s code security and secret risk assessments now indicate whether findings are in protected or unprotected repositories, helping organizations spot where to extend security coverage. The improvement is available in GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Team; secret risk assessment support is slated for GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows weekly update highlights hardening and cost-aware routing
items.content_text: GitHub’s November 2 Agentic Workflows roundup describes safer pull-request outputs, optional actions-lock integration, guided remediation, and additional workflows adopting model routing to keep lower-cost work economical. The post reports these project updates and notes that release v1.0.1 itself was published October 27.

items.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors program to support strained power grids
items.content_text: OpenAI launched Grid Protectors, a national program to work with utilities, regulators, and policymakers on reducing electricity demand at its future campuses during periods of grid strain. In Georgia, the company says its planned Effingham County campus agreement includes up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response; additional arrangements will vary by location.

items.title: OpenAI signs Abu Dhabi agreements on AI investment and UAE-wide adoption
items.content_text: Abu Dhabi announced new agreements involving OpenAI, including an AI investment-analysis arrangement with Mubadala and Inception42, and a five-year agreement with Inception42 to support frontier AI adoption across government, enterprise, and education. The announcement signals a wider regional expansion of OpenAI’s institutional partnerships beyond the separate ADNOC energy deal.

items.title: ADNOC partners with OpenAI and G42 to deploy Frontier across its energy operations
items.content_text: ADNOC, OpenAI, and G42 announced a multi-year partnership to deploy OpenAI Frontier across ADNOC’s energy operations, making ADNOC the first energy company to deploy the platform. The partners plan to combine OpenAI models with ADNOC’s industrial data on G42’s sovereign UAE infrastructure to support planning and connected business decisions, with human experts overseeing consequential decisions.

items.title: Omen AI acquires Aquatic Labs for $16 million to advance data-center cooling
items.content_text: Omen AI announced a $16 million cash-and-stock acquisition of Aquatic Labs, adding its sensor research and expertise to Omen’s AI data-center cooling systems. The companies plan to combine fluid-monitoring capabilities to help operators detect cooling problems earlier and reduce disruption.

items.title: Grok Bot usage limits tightened amid high operating costs
items.content_text: Grok Bot users reported reaching usage limits sooner, and Elon Musk said the cost of serving the AI agent was “unsustainably high relative to revenue.” The episode points to the operational and commercial costs of running always-on agents, though the exact changes to limits were not detailed in the cited report.

items.title: 42AI emerges from stealth with $62.5 million for behavioral world model
items.content_text: Israeli startup 42AI came out of stealth with $62.5 million in seed funding to develop a model intended to predict human behavior. The company says its system is already being used at some financial brokerages, though its performance claims remain early-stage and company-reported.

items.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx benchmark for agentic AI capabilities
items.content_text: SemiAnalysis introduced GDPx, a benchmark for agentic capabilities across domains including software engineering, finance, law, biology, and chip design. The release adds a new evaluation framework for comparing AI agents on high-value professional work.

items.title: OpenAI merges ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs while sharing usage allowance with Codex
items.content_text: OpenAI is merging ChatGPT’s Chat and Work tabs and moving ChatGPT and Codex to a shared token allowance pool, while keeping Codex separate in the desktop app. The change may affect how often some users need to wait for usage resets.

items.title: Salesforce adds agent evaluations and cost controls to Agent Fabric
items.content_text: Salesforce expanded Agent Fabric with Agent Evals and API Evals to test agent quality and API changes, plus cost controls that can impose hard budget limits and reduce token usage. The additions are aimed at catching silent failures and overspending as organizations put more agents into production; Agent Evals and API Evals are scheduled for beta in November 2026 and general availability in January 2027.

items.title: Google DeepMind expands Gemini-powered PlanAssist to 12 more councils
items.content_text: Google DeepMind is expanding its Gemini-powered PlanAssist tool to 12 additional local planning authorities in England, bringing the total involved to 15 for a 12-month beta using live applications. Early pilots reported a 58% reduction in time spent on householder application assessments, while qualified planning officers retain final approval.

items.title: Google showcases Gemini 4 Argon agents building a dancing robot from a prompt
items.content_text: Google highlighted a Google DeepMind robotics project in which AI agents powered by Gemini 4 Argon and Antigravity helped create a physical, dancing 12-degree-of-freedom robot from a plain-English prompt. The demonstration is a notable example of Gemini-powered agents being used in a real-world robotics workflow without manual CAD.

items.title: DeepSeek releases open-source Super-Agent coding prototype
items.content_text: DeepSeek published dsh-superagent, an MIT-licensed research prototype that can work on a GitHub repository and optionally listen to Feishu. The project is explicitly labeled as reference research code—not an official DeepSeek product or production-ready software—while its proactive, low-attention agent design reflects growing competition in AI coding tools.

items.title: Microsoft summarizes October Azure Developer CLI releases and features
items.content_text: Microsoft’s October Azure Developer CLI roundup covers releases 1.35.0 through 1.37.2. Highlights include deployment previews across multiple Azure services, Container Apps express deployments, a beta command for removing stored environment values, and support for extension-defined infrastructure providers in generated pipelines.

items.title: OpenAI and Google back a shared website signal for AI-training preferences
items.content_text: OpenAI and Google announced support for a shared robots.txt signal through which publishers and website operators can communicate AI-training preferences to multiple participating providers at once. The initiative is voluntary and still being implemented; OpenAI says its existing crawler controls will remain in place.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.316 adds subagent and gateway controls and deprecates Opus 4.8 fast mode
items.content_text: Claude Code 2.1.316 adds configurable subagent effort, an option to disable the “ultrathink” keyword, and pooled group budgets and policy controls for the Claude apps gateway. It also deprecates Opus 4.8 fast mode as of October 30, with removal scheduled for November 30, 2026.

items.title: Google DeepMind and WRI create AI-based global forest map
items.content_text: Google DeepMind and the World Resources Institute developed ForTy, a global map that classifies 2020 land cover into six categories at 10-meter resolution using satellite data and AI. The reported overall accuracy was 90.2%, though the article notes weaker identification of some tree crops and plantations, relevant limitations for land-use monitoring.

items.title: Estée Lauder expands Copilot access to more than 14,000 employees
items.content_text: Estée Lauder expanded Microsoft Copilot access across its office-based global workforce of more than 14,000 people. The deployment is part of a broader effort to bring Microsoft AI and cloud tools into the company’s business operations.

items.title: Microsoft announces new Windows 11 Insider builds and private Feedback Hub policy
items.content_text: Microsoft released new Windows 11 Insider builds to the Beta and Experimental channels and introduced an Intune policy that can keep tenant users’ Feedback Hub submissions private. The accompanying previews include expanded Windows Search actions and, in a Future Platforms build, app-by-app camera, microphone, and location permissions for desktop apps.

items.title: GitHub app in Microsoft Teams reaches general availability
items.content_text: The GitHub app in Microsoft Teams is now generally available, letting teams work with GitHub and Copilot in the context of their chats, channels, and meeting chats. Users can ask in natural language to select or switch repositories and choose which Copilot model to use for a task.

items.title: Claude renames its Max plans and removes the five-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts
items.content_text: Anthropic renamed Max 5x to Max and Max 20x to Ultra without changing their $100 and $200 monthly prices. Verified Ultra accounts no longer have a five-hour usage limit, while weekly limits remain; the plans also include monthly Claude Platform API credits.

items.title: OpenAI highlights support for fair use in AI training
items.content_text: OpenAI published a collection of arguments from authors, academics, legal experts, and other groups supporting the application of fair use to AI training. The post presents this as support for OpenAI’s position in ongoing copyright debates; it is advocacy and commentary, not a new court decision.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Rosalind for specialized life-sciences research
items.content_text: OpenAI released GPT-6 Rosalind, a model for specialized biological reasoning and scientific tool use in life-sciences research. OpenAI says it has additional deployment controls for advanced research and retains trusted-access eligibility requirements, rather than broadening access.

items.title: OpenAI announces new community-safety reporting and protections for teens
items.content_text: OpenAI announced tighter ChatGPT restrictions on firearms-related content for minors and a Community Safety Report covering violence prevention and other community-safety issues. The first report is planned for early 2027, with updates every six months, making this a substantive update to both product safeguards and public reporting.

items.title: Claude-based AI agent selects gene therapy and performs a mouse-brain procedure
items.content_text: A Claude Sonnet 5 agent reportedly selected a gene therapy, brain target, and injection coordinates, then controlled a motorized rig during a procedure on a mouse. The agent stopped after detecting a calibration error; the account was attributed to Exin Therapeutics’ co-founder, and the report noted that the results had not been peer-reviewed.

items.title: OpenAI’s latest funding round falls short of its initial $30 billion target
items.content_text: The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI had secured roughly $11 billion in commitments toward an initially planned $30 billion funding round, at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation versus an earlier $1.4 trillion target. TechCrunch, citing the Financial Times and WSJ, said OpenAI lowered its fundraising target to $20 billion and that the initial close may fall below that amount.

items.title: OpenAI introduces restricted GPT-Rosalind-6 for life-sciences research
items.content_text: OpenAI published GPT-Rosalind-6, a reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine, for qualified research organizations through a trusted-access program. The model is intended to be more useful for legitimate advanced biological research, including some dual-use topics, while retaining access review and deployment safeguards.

items.title: Microsoft’s October Copilot roundup details product and admin updates
items.content_text: Microsoft’s October Copilot roundup highlights updates across Cowork, SharePoint, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, and administration. Among the changes are role-based Cowork plugins and a task catalog, a SharePoint knowledge base, Excel accounting skills, and Insights Agent capabilities for analyzing agent usage and feedback; some features are rolling out globally in November.

items.title: Gemini API Computer Use reaches general availability
items.content_text: Google made the Computer Use tool generally available across the Gemini Interactions API and GenerateContent API. This moves the capability beyond its earlier preview status and makes it available for production use through both API surfaces.

items.title: UK CMA investigates Meta’s commercial terms for using publishers’ content in AI products
items.content_text: The UK CMA opened an investigation into whether Meta’s commercial terms for businesses and publishers could breach competition law by allowing Meta to collect and use their website content in its products, including AI features. The regulator has not made a finding that Meta broke the law; it will gather evidence from Meta and affected third parties.

items.title: Microsoft expands Copilot with finance skills and partner-built plugins
items.content_text: Microsoft announced more than 25 finance skills and partner-built plugins for accounting, capital markets, and other finance work. Accounting capabilities in Copilot in Excel and Cowork are available in Frontier, while the Capital Markets and Finance plugins for Cowork are generally available; Dynamics 365 ERP and partner plugins are beginning to roll out.

items.title: Microsoft Intune October updates add security baselines, EPM network controls, and Autopatch scheduling
items.content_text: Microsoft’s October Intune updates add a Windows 365 for Agents security baseline and let standard users make IT-approved network-setting changes through Endpoint Privilege Management without broad admin rights. Windows Autopatch also gains expanded approval and scheduling controls for quality updates, including independent management of different update types.

items.title: Microsoft updates KB5127936 notes with modernized AutoPlay details and a Windows 11 24H2 update clarification
items.content_text: Microsoft’s KB5127936 notes were updated on October 29 to detail a modernized AutoPlay experience, including dark mode, improved text scaling, and notifications in Notification Center. The notes also clarify that Windows 11 24H2 no longer receives non-security preview updates starting with the October 2026 release; Enterprise and Education editions continue to receive monthly security updates.

items.title: Microsoft Edge adds accelerated app launches on Windows 11
items.content_text: Microsoft announced that Edge is the first browser to support Windows accelerated app launches, with a stated 15% launch-speed improvement for most users and up to 33% under heavy multitasking. The capability is supported with Edge 150 or later on Windows 11 versions 25H2, 26H2, and 26H1 when KB5127936 or a later update is installed.

items.title: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11.3 addresses security advisories
items.content_text: Microsoft released Visual Studio 2026 version 18.11.3 on October 29 with security advisory fixes. The listed issues include a libcurl HTTP/2 upload use-after-free, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write, and a Visual Studio certificate-validation vulnerability.

items.title: GitHub adds webhook delivery IP ranges to the Meta API
items.content_text: GitHub added three webhook delivery IP ranges to the Meta API’s `hooks` field. Operators maintaining static allowlists should add the prefixes to avoid rejecting deliveries; the change applies across GitHub.com plans, including Enterprise Cloud.

items.title: Microsoft details vcpkg’s October update, including configurable cache compression
items.content_text: Microsoft summarized October changes to vcpkg, including a configurable binary-cache compression level, improved cache diagnostics and reliability, and updated ports such as Boost 1.92.0. The compression option lets developers trade ZIP archive size against cache submission time.

items.title: Anthropic describes Claude’s self-assessment system for flagging potential misuse
items.content_text: Anthropic publicly described Claude’s “self-assessment” mechanism, which produces a preliminary safety assessment after a response and can flag potential misuse. The company said it had used the technique since June and that it had surfaced misuse not caught by other safeguards; it is described as one safety signal, not as a replacement for broader safeguards.

items.title: Claude API request-size limit increases from 32 MB to 128 MB
items.content_text: Anthropic increased the first-party Claude API’s maximum request size for Messages and Token Counting from 32 MB to 128 MB, giving image-heavy requests such as large PDFs and computer-use sessions more headroom. For requests with more than 20 images, it also raised the per-image limit from 2,000 to 3,000 pixels; cloud-hosted platforms have separate limits.

items.title: Claude announces mobile-app upgrades, multi-account switching, and 24 additional languages
items.content_text: Claude announced several app improvements, including a side-by-side/full-screen experience on iPad and iPhone Duo, multiple-account switching on iOS and Android, and laptop-style Android support on Chromebooks and foldables. Claude also added 24 languages across web, desktop, iOS, and Android, bringing the total to 33.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.166.0 adds transcript search and model catalog support
items.content_text: Codex CLI 0.166.0 adds keyboard-driven transcript selection with integrated search and configurable shortcuts, adds GPT-6.1 Terra to bundled, Vertex AI, and Amazon Bedrock catalogs, and introduces clearer safety-block explanations plus network-only diagnostics. These changes improve transcript navigation and broaden model/provider and troubleshooting support for Codex users.

items.title: OpenAI updates its Model Spec around five core values
items.content_text: OpenAI reorganized its public model-behavior guidance around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. The update also adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency and adjusts some behavioral defaults, making it a substantive change to OpenAI’s stated approach to model behavior.

items.title: OpenAI details expanded monitoring for frontier-model misalignment
items.content_text: OpenAI published details of its expanded system for monitoring frontier models for misalignment and potentially unauthorized agent behavior. The company says it evaluates monitoring performance against recorded incidents and simulated attacks, and tracks recall before deploying changes; the disclosure matters because it explains how OpenAI aims to identify and investigate concerning model behavior.

items.title: Ropes & Gray develops transactional-diligence AI with OpenAI
items.content_text: Ropes & Gray is developing a proprietary OpenAI-powered tool for the first pass of commercial contract diligence. It reviews and groups documents, generates summaries and a report in the firm’s format, and is intended to help lawyers move from document review to client advice more quickly while preserving lawyer judgment.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities
items.content_text: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model it says improves coding, agentic work, and cybersecurity defense, including vulnerability detection and patching. The company says access will initially focus on cyber defenders, making this a notable release of advanced AI capabilities with a restricted initial audience.

items.title: Copilot in SharePoint adds generally available image, analytics, and metadata tools
items.content_text: Microsoft says advanced Copilot in SharePoint capabilities are now generally available, including image generation and editing, AI-generated site analytics reports, and near-real-time metadata autofill. The features use Copilot Credits and are available to Copilot-licensed users, adding new AI-assisted workflows across SharePoint sites and document libraries.

items.title: Microsoft and Syncfusion collaborate on open-source Blazor toolkit and contributions
items.content_text: Microsoft announced a collaboration with Syncfusion to advance Blazor. Syncfusion has released a free, MIT-licensed component toolkit and contributed fixes and tests to ASP.NET Core and .NET scaffolding, adding reusable components while contributing directly to the platform.

items.title: SentinelOne plans to add Claude Mythos 5.1 to its Wayfinder security service
items.content_text: SentinelOne announced plans to add Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5.1 to Wayfinder Frontier AI Services, where it will be used alongside security experts to help identify and assess software risks. The announcement is a new security-services partnership development; SentinelOne described the addition as upcoming rather than already available.

items.title: Anthropic expands AI for Science support to foundations and research institutions
items.content_text: Anthropic expanded its AI for Science program beyond individual researchers, partnering with 20 scientific foundations, institutions, and research groups and providing Claude credits for research. The announcement also highlights collaborations on safe lab-instrument use and AI-assisted analysis of scientific datasets, broadening the program’s institutional reach.

items.title: Gemini adds in-chat document creation, preview, and editing
items.content_text: Gemini now lets users create, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, code, and other files within a chat. Google says PDF preview and editing are available on web and mobile, while other listed formats are currently web-only; the capabilities are available to all Gemini app users in supported regions and languages.

items.title: Google reports Gemini classroom-study findings from the UK and Italy
items.content_text: Google shared findings from studies in the UK and Italy on Gemini’s use in classrooms. The UK trial found AI tutoring provided math support comparable to human tutors for many students; the Italy study reported higher participation and more student-led collaboration when teachers used Gemini to co-design lessons.

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter Large 4 model
items.content_text: Mistral released the weights for its improved Large 4 (Le Chonk), a one-trillion-parameter multimodal model, after additional training beyond its earlier public preview. The release emphasizes agentic coding, defensive cybersecurity, and self-hosting; the model is available under Mistral’s Ecosystem Open-Weight license, which includes a separate-license condition for some model-as-a-service uses.

items.title: Deepgram to acquire Daily, makers of open-source voice-agent framework Pipecat
items.content_text: Deepgram announced it is acquiring Daily, the company behind the open-source Pipecat voice-agent framework, to combine it with Deepgram’s voice AI infrastructure. The companies say Pipecat will remain open source and vendor neutral; they did not disclose the deal amount.

items.title: Cohere announces initial Series E close targeting up to CAD $7 billion
items.content_text: Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E round targeting up to CAD $7 billion, a figure the company says would imply a CAD $35.7 billion valuation. Schwarz Group is the lead investor; Cohere says the financing will support compute infrastructure, frontier models, and AI products for enterprises and governments, but the target is not the same as the amount already committed.

items.title: Digital Science acquires Jenni AI, bringing its AI research-writing platform into its scholarly-data ecosystem
items.content_text: Digital Science acquired Jenni AI, an AI-native research and writing platform used by more than 8 million students and researchers in 189 countries. The planned integration with Digital Science’s research data, starting with its Dimensions database, aims to connect AI-assisted discovery and writing with published research sources and citation checking.

items.title: Windows 11 26H1 preview adds WinRE remote-management support for MDM providers
items.content_text: Microsoft’s October 28 preview update KB5127653 for Windows 11 version 26H1 adds a recovery remote-management plug-in that extends Windows Recovery Environment management capabilities for MDM providers. The update also includes other Windows improvements, but this new MDM recovery capability is the notable endpoint-management change.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot harness enters public preview in Foundry Agent Service
items.content_text: Microsoft introduced the Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service as a public preview, giving developers a managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. The post also announced general availability of long-running resilience for hosted agents.

items.title: Visual Studio Marketplace adds secretless Trusted Publishing for extensions
items.content_text: Microsoft announced Trusted Publishing for Visual Studio Marketplace extensions. GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines can use verified federated identity to publish without storing a long-lived personal access token or publishing secret; existing PAT-based publishing remains available.

items.title: Microsoft makes Copilot UX components generally available with SPFx 1.24
items.content_text: Microsoft made Copilot UX components generally available worldwide with SharePoint Framework 1.24, allowing developers to bring interactive dashboards, forms, and business actions into Copilot conversations. Components can also be reused in SharePoint, Teams, and Outlook; users need a Microsoft Copilot add-on license to render them in Copilot.

items.title: Copilot code review adds Max effort preview and generally available approvals
items.content_text: GitHub added a Max effort level for Copilot code review in public preview and made Copilot approvals generally available. The combination is intended to provide a deeper review and an approval assessment within the pull-request review workflow.

items.title: Visual Studio Code 1.144 stable release expands agent workflows and continuity
items.content_text: VS Code 1.144 shipped in the stable channel with expanded agent workflows, including agent sessions that continue across environments and client continuity supported by the Agent Host Protocol. The release also brings agent management and model-selection updates, making it a substantial IDE update for developers using Copilot agents.

items.title: GitHub brings Copilot Agent Merge into cloud pull requests
items.content_text: GitHub integrated Agent Merge into pull requests on GitHub.com. Copilot can watch for blockers such as failing Actions workflows and merge conflicts and attempt to fix them; the cloud feature is available to paid Copilot users subject to organization and enterprise policies.

items.title: IDC brings its Quanta research platform into Claude and adopts Claude company-wide
items.content_text: Anthropic and IDC brought IDC Quanta into Claude, letting IDC customers query the research platform’s forecasts, market data, and analysis through Claude. IDC also rolled Claude out across its own business, combining a customer-facing research integration with a significant enterprise adoption.

items.title: Anthropic makes smart reports, surveys, and pooled budgets generally available for Claude Enterprise
items.content_text: Anthropic made smart reports, in-app surveys, and pooled group budgets generally available for Claude Enterprise. The features give organizations new ways to understand Claude usage and outcomes, gather employee feedback, and set shared team spending limits.

items.title: ChatGPT begins beta texting for dot agents via iMessage and RCS
items.content_text: OpenAI began rolling out texting for its dot agent through iMessage and RCS, allowing users to send text, photos, and voice messages and receive proactive updates. The beta preview is for ChatGPT Pro users in the U.S., extending access to the agent beyond the ChatGPT app.

items.title: FuriosaAI raises $620 million in Series D at $2.9 billion valuation
items.content_text: South Korean AI-chip company FuriosaAI announced a $620 million Series D at a $2.9 billion post-money valuation. It said the funding will support production and deployment of its RNGD inference accelerator, software development, and work on a third-generation accelerator.

items.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion reaches general availability for model routing
items.content_text: Copilot Fusion is now generally available, letting users delegate model selection and orchestration to Copilot instead of choosing a model for each task. It is available across all Copilot plans in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot CLI, and JetBrains IDEs, with Standard, High, and Max effort levels.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 fixes Fusion effort selection in long-context sessions
items.content_text: Copilot CLI 1.0.105 fixes an issue that prevented users from selecting Copilot Fusion High or Max from /model during long-context sessions. The official release page records publication on October 28.

items.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows reaches general availability
items.content_text: GitHub Agentic Workflows is generally available on GitHub.com for Free, Team, and Enterprise. It lets users define reasoning-based automations in Markdown for compilation into GitHub Actions workflows, with GA additions including self-hosted runner support, improved budget forecasting, model routing, and stronger agent isolation.

items.title: Copilot Fusion previews intelligent routing between local and cloud models
items.content_text: Copilot Fusion’s experimental preview can route requests between supported on-device and cloud models in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code. The announcement includes managed Windows setup for MAI Code 1.1 Flash and support for manually configured local models; it notes that routing still makes decisions in the cloud.

items.title: GitHub Copilot app adds Projects and computer use in public preview
items.content_text: The GitHub Copilot app introduced Projects in public preview, providing a home for work spanning repositories and sessions. It also announced computer use in public preview on macOS and Windows, allowing Copilot to interact with desktop applications, including apps without APIs or MCP integrations.

items.title: GitHub Enterprise begins including access to Copilot for licensed users
items.content_text: GitHub Enterprise customers working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can now include Copilot access for each licensed user, with AI-credit budgeting applying to some capabilities. This changes how eligible enterprises manage Copilot access, while self-serve subscriptions remain unaffected and will receive availability in stages.

items.title: GitHub Copilot previews natural-language image generation and editing
items.content_text: Copilot users can now generate and edit images with natural-language instructions without leaving Copilot. The feature is in public preview for Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise plans, with image-token usage billed separately and counted against plan AI credits.

items.title: GitHub rolls out shared Copilot Automations for teams
items.content_text: Shared Copilot Automations let teams build and maintain AI-powered workflows together in repositories. Automations are visible to repository readers, editable by those with write access, and billed to the repository owner; GitHub says rollout is underway for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans.

items.title: GitHub introduces intelligence features for Copilot memory, context, and code search
items.content_text: GitHub announced a context and learning layer for agents, including Copilot Memory, now generally available on paid plans, and Copilot dreaming, in public preview. Memory can carry personal preferences and repository conventions across sessions and clients, while dreaming reviews prior work to improve future agent sessions.

items.title: GitHub previews a Security extension for the Copilot app
items.content_text: GitHub introduced a public-preview Security extension in the Copilot app that surfaces repository code-scanning alerts and lets users ask Copilot to explain or help fix them. The preview is available on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency; Enterprise Server is not supported.

items.title: Anthropic adds ready-to-use legal artifacts to Claude for Legal
items.content_text: Anthropic added a gallery of ready-to-use interactive artifacts for Claude for Legal, including tools for contract review, regulatory tracking, and routing legal requests. Legal teams can adapt and share the tools using their own data and connectors, extending Claude Enterprise’s workflow options for legal work.

items.title: OpenAI spotlights Legora’s legal-work AI platform and use of OpenAI products
items.content_text: OpenAI profiled Legora’s legal AI platform, which uses OpenAI models for workflows including agentic legal work and document review. The article also notes Legora’s use of ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots, illustrating the company’s products across both customer-facing software and internal operations.

items.title: NVIDIA releases open-weight Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe speech model and Granary v2 dataset
items.content_text: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open-weight speech model that combines multilingual transcription, speaker attribution, translation and audio Q&A, and paired it with the open Granary v2 speech dataset. The release gives developers a single model and dataset resources for building or adapting speech applications, including workplace and medical use cases.

items.title: Akeneo expands governed AI-agent product workflows and acquires Dataggo
items.content_text: Akeneo announced new agent-enabled product-data workflows with enterprise controls, including Ziggy for Shopify and additional supplier-data capabilities, and said the Autumn Release was available starting October 28. The company also announced its acquisition of Dataggo, an AI-native product-information-management services specialist, to strengthen enterprise deployments.
